introduction.text: The Mausoleo di Sant'Urbano martire is a Roman mausoleum located at the IV mile of the Appian Way in Rome, notable for its early Christian burial practices and subsequent transformations through history.

history.description: Construction of the mausoleum during the Antonine period, in the 2nd century AD.
Demolition of the original staircase during Diocleziano's persecution (late 3rd to early 4th century) and subsequent reconstruction with a more majestic facade and a tetrastilo portico.
The mausoleum served as a Christian cemetery until the Gothic invasions in the 5th century.
Transformation of the mausoleum into a fortified tower (torrione dei Borgiani) in the 13th century.
Excavations conducted by the Lugari in the late 19th century, revealing the Domus Marmeniae and other archaeological features.
Use of the mausoleum as a Christian burial site after the death of Marmenia, with remains of Sant'Urbano transferred from the Catacombs of Pretestato.

design.description: The mausoleum consists of an underground hypogeum and an upper hall for worship.
The original entrance was via a staircase inside the vestibule, which was demolished during Diocleziano's persecution and later rebuilt with a more majestic facade and a tetrastilo portico.
The hypogeum features a vestibule and a large square chamber with three apses: a central semicircular apse and two rectangular side apses.
In the 13th century, the mausoleum was converted into a fortified tower known as the 'torrione dei Borgiani'.
A large Roman cistern and basin were found near the monument.
